contexts.description:
The contexts in which this action can be performed. For example, a weapon
attack can be performed in the context of a melee or ranged attack. If left
empty, the default context is used, which is appropriate for actions like
`Dash` or `Action Surge`, which don't require a specific context

^([A-Za-z0-9_]+::)?resource[A-Za-z0-9_.].description: A flat amount (`1`) or a tiered amount `<tier>:<amount>` (e.g. `2:1` for one level-2 spell slot).

target_usability.description:
Checked once a target has been chosen, for conditions that depend on who is
being targeted (e.g. Brutal Strike needs Advantage against *this* target)

attack_roll.description: How the attack roll is made.

saving_throw.description: `<dc provider>;<ability>` where the DC provider is `spell_save_dc`, `weapon_save_dc`, or `spell_save_dc(<class id>)` for a class feature that uses that class's spell save DC outside a spell, e.g. `spell_save_dc;dexterity`.

anyOf.description:
Made by the actor rather than the target, and succeeds when the check
does (e.g. Help's DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check to stabilize a creature)

ActionContext.description: Represents the context in which an action is performed.

item.description: The carried item the action uses up, e.g. a potion

ActionId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]action.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::action.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

phases.description: The phases every variant shares, run before the chosen variant's own

body.description: Script id of a Lua reaction body, e.g. `nat20_core::script.shield`, or the built-in `cancel_event`.

damage.description: Damage roll: `<dice expression>;<damage type>` (e.g. `8d6;fire`, `(1 + spell_level)d6;cold`) or `attack_context` to derive the damage roll from the used attack context. Expressions may use the variables `spell_level`, `caster_level`, `character_level` and `<class>.level` (e.g. `class.wizard.level`).

Damage roll: `<dice expression>;<damage type>` (e.g. `8d6;fire`, `(1 + spell_level)d6;cold`) or `attack_context` to derive the damage roll from the used attack context. Expressions may use the variables `spell_level`, `caster_level`, `character_level` and `<class>.level` (e.g. `class.wizard.level`).

healing.description: Healing roll as a dice expression. Expressions may use the variables `spell_level`, `caster_level`, `character_level` and `<class>.level` (e.g. `class.wizard.level`).

reaction.description: Script id of a Lua reaction body, e.g. `nat20_core::script.shield`, or the built-in `cancel_event`.

anyOf.description: Changes the target's life state when the condition succeeds

requires.description: Gate on the previous phase's condition outcome (per target)

oneOf.description: The actor must be proficient in this skill

ActionVariantId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]variant.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::variant.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

oneOf.description: Remove the effect instance when the event fires

Re-roll the applying action's condition and remove the effect on a
success (e.g. Hold Person's repeat save)

against.description:
Who the roll is made against. Only attack rolls have a target, so a
filter with `against` never matches saving throws or skill checks.

roller.description: Who makes the roll. Omit to match any roller.

skill.description:
Only match checks made with this skill (e.g. Help's Advantage is spent
by the next check with the chosen skill). Omit to match any skill.

events.description: Event kinds this filter can match

EffectId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]effect.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::effect.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

EffectLifetimeTemplate.description:
Effect lifetimes are unique in the sense that they can refer to different entities,
but those entities are only known at runtime. Therefore, we need a template
that can be instantiated into a concrete `EffectLifetime` when the effect is applied.

oneOf.description:
An entity has declared they want to take an action. The engine can then
validate that the entity can perform the action and either approve or
deny it. Other entities might also react to the request, e.g. if someone
is casting a spell, another entity might use their reaction to Counterspell
the action.

The result of performing an action.
Despite the name it can also be used outside of actions.
TODO: Maybe a better name then?
The initial D20 roll which can be reacted to, e.g. with the Lucky feat.
The final result of a D20 check after reactions have been applied.

FeatId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]feat.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::feat.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

ItemId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]item.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::item.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

LifeStateChange.description:
A change to a creature's life state that an action makes directly, rather
than through damage or healing.

oneOf.description:
"A Stable creature doesn't make Death Saving Throws even though it has 0
Hit Points, but it still has the Unconscious condition." Only a creature
that is making Death Saving Throws can become Stable; any other creature
is unaffected.

launch_velocity.description: `<integer expression> <unit>` (e.g. `10 + spell_level ft` for a length) where the unit is one of `m/s`, `ft/s`, `km/h`, `mph`. Expressions may use the variables `spell_level`, `caster_level`, `character_level` and `<class>.level` (e.g. `class.wizard.level`).

velocity.description: `<integer expression> <unit>` (e.g. `10 + spell_level ft` for a length) where the unit is one of `m/s`, `ft/s`, `km/h`, `mph`. Expressions may use the variables `spell_level`, `caster_level`, `character_level` and `<class>.level` (e.g. `class.wizard.level`).

PhaseRequirement.description:
In case of multiple phases, this describes the requirement for a phase to be
executed, e.g. only execute if the previous phase succeeded or failed.

events.description:
Event kinds that can trigger this reaction, checked before the
trigger script runs.

script.description: Script id of a Lua reaction trigger, e.g. `nat20_core::script.shield`.

ScriptId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]script.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::script.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

SkillCheckDefinition.description:
A skill check the actor makes against a fixed DC, e.g. "a successful DC 10
Wisdom (Medicine) check" to stabilize a creature

dc.description: The DC the check has to meet or beat to succeed

skill.description: The skill the actor makes the check with

SpeciesId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]species.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::species.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

SpellId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]spell.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::spell.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

SubclassId.description: Registry id `[namespace::]subclass.<name>`, e.g. `nat20_core::subclass.example`. The namespace defaults to `nat20_core`.

range.description: `<integer expression> <unit>` (e.g. `10 + spell_level ft` for a length) where the unit is one of `m`/`meter(s)`, `ft`/`foot`/`feet`. Expressions may use the variables `spell_level`, `caster_level`, `character_level` and `<class>.level` (e.g. `class.wizard.level`).

max_targets.description: Integer expression. Expressions may use the variables `spell_level`, `caster_level`, `character_level` and `<class>.level` (e.g. `class.wizard.level`).

time.description: `<integer expression> <unit>` (e.g. `10 + spell_level ft` for a length) where the unit is one of `s`/`sec`/`second(s)`, `min`/`minute(s)`, `hr`/`hour(s)`. Expressions may use the variables `spell_level`, `caster_level`, `character_level` and `<class>.level` (e.g. `class.wizard.level`).
